## Caption (verbatim)

```
This post speaks to the seasons when God feels silent and the provision in front of you seems to be disappearing.

Elijah was one of the boldest prophets in all of Scripture. He called down fire from heaven. He confronted kings. But before any of that — God sent him to sit beside a brook in the middle of nowhere. No audience. No miracles. Just water that was slowly running out.

And God said nothing.

That silence was not cruelty. It was formation. Every day Elijah stayed at that drying brook, his dependence on God deepened. He could not rely on the water — it was disappearing. He could not rely on his own plan — he had none. All he had was the instruction to stay.

Most of us know this season. The prayer that hits the ceiling. The relationship that is not healing on your timeline. The calling that feels like it dried up months ago. And the hardest part is not the struggle — it is the silence around it.

But here is what Elijah's story teaches: God was never absent. While the brook dried up, God was already preparing the widow of Zarephath. The next provision was being positioned before the current one ran out. Elijah just could not see it yet.

You are not forgotten in the waiting. You are being prepared in it.

SCRIPTURE:
"But those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint."
— Isaiah 40:31 (NKJV)
```
